metadata.batch: Batch 24 + D49.6 (D49 pop-out robustness: restore, attach, host error, fan-out, hold verify, tz handoff)
metadata.note: P13: D49.1-D49.7 over waves W1-W8. T1 restore (M) -> T2 transactional attach (M) -> T3 host error (S) -> T4 single fan-out (S) -> T5 hold probe+record, no prod change (S) -> T6 conditional per-owner fix or verified-close (S) -> T7 tz create threading (S) -> T8 tz persist/restore/fallback (S) -> T9 batch gate (S). Strict chain per plan wave order. Repro-first everywhere except T4 pin-green-first and T6 record-gated. No skips/xfails; no order code; Qt-free data/services boundary held; full suite green.

tasks.title: Cold restore routes through cached bars + aggregator + realtime subscribe (D49.1)
tasks.description: Extend ui/main_window.py _restore_popouts with a data-path ensure step: for a saved pop-out whose symbol has no in-memory session, load cached bars via BarCache, create the timeframe BarAggregator, and realtime-subscribe; where cache coverage is incomplete, issue the existing history/backfill/pacing requests (A121, cache-first per R96). Already-loaded main-chart symbols add nothing; disconnected restore stays a D14-style no-op. Covers S-P13-1, AC-D49.1.
acceptance_criteria: Given a saved pop-out for a symbol with no in-memory session and a seeded BarCache, when the restore path runs offscreen, then the window shows the cached bars, owns the timeframe aggregator, and holds a realtime subscription.

Given a saved pop-out whose seeded cache has a gapped span, when the restore path runs offscreen, then it issues the existing backfill/pacing request covering the gap instead of leaving the window stale.

Given a saved pop-out for the already-loaded main-chart symbol, when the restore path runs, then no second aggregator and no second subscription is created; and given a disconnected client, when restore runs, then it stays a status-message no-op issuing no request.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given a saved pop-out for a symbol with no in-memory session and a seeded BarCache, when the restore path runs offscreen, then the window shows the cached bars, owns the timeframe aggregator, and holds a realtime subscription.
tests.description: Seed BarCache for an unloaded symbol, run _restore_popouts offscreen with mocked IBKR, assert the pop-out view bars equal the seeded bars, the timeframe aggregator exists on the session, and a realtime hold is held. Red pre-fix (empty/stale window).
tests.expected_result: Fails pre-fix (no bars/aggregator/subscription on the cold path); passes post-fix.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given a saved pop-out whose seeded cache has a gapped span, when the restore path runs offscreen, then it issues the existing backfill/pacing request covering the gap instead of leaving the window stale.
tests.description: Seed a gapped cache, stub req_historical_data to record calls, run _restore_popouts, assert a backfill request covering the missing span is issued through the existing path.
tests.expected_result: Fails pre-fix (no request issued); passes post-fix.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given a saved pop-out for the already-loaded main-chart symbol, when the restore path runs, then no second aggregator and no second subscription is created; and given a disconnected client, when restore runs, then it stays a status-message no-op issuing no request.
tests.description: Restore a pop-out for the loaded symbol and assert aggregator/subscription identity is unchanged; restore while disconnected and assert a status message with zero historical/RT requests.
tests.expected_result: Passes post-fix; any duplicate aggregator, duplicate subscription, or disconnected request fails it.

tasks.title: Transactional attach with explicit acquisition-state tracking (D49.2)
tasks.description: Rewrite ui/popout_window.py PopoutChartWindow.attach as a transaction: record each acquired step (connected signals, attached view, RT hold only where ensure_rt_subscribed returned, registration, resources) and on ANY failure unwind in reverse order, releasing only the hold this attach acquired. detach_view is reused unchanged (frozen). Covers S-P13-2, AC-D49.2.
acceptance_criteria: Given each attach failure-injection point (sync raise, registration raise, save raise), when attach fails offscreen, then the session holds no stale view, the realtime hold count is unchanged by the failed attach, the pop-out is unregistered, and the connected signals are disconnected.
Given a shared live session with other attached views, when one pop-out attach fails offscreen, then the surviving views keep their session membership, holds, and updates undisturbed.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given each attach failure-injection point (sync raise, registration raise, save raise), when attach fails offscreen, then the session holds no stale view, the realtime hold count is unchanged by the failed attach, the pop-out is unregistered, and the connected signals are disconnected.
tests.description: Per-injection-point cases (monkeypatched sync/registration/save raising): assert session-view membership excludes the failed view, hold count delta is zero, registry membership is absent, and signal connections are torn down. Red pre-fix (leaked view/hold/registration).
tests.expected_result: Fail pre-fix; green post-fix for every injection point.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given a shared live session with other attached views, when one pop-out attach fails offscreen, then the surviving views keep their session membership, holds, and updates undisturbed.
tests.description: Two-view session, fail the second attach (attach-failure-under-update ordering per R97: disconnect-signals-first), assert the first view still receives session updates with its hold intact.
tests.expected_result: Green post-fix; any disturbed survivor fails it.

Given the rendered error state, when compared against the no-data state and the ESC-070 wording, then the state is unambiguous versus no-data and the message text reuses the chart_engine_failure_message wording without rewording.

tasks.title: Pin drawing fan-out baseline, then synchronize once at the change point (D49.4)
tasks.description: First land pinning tests on the current tree recording per-change sync_drawings_to_views fan-out count and end state (green-first by design), then de-duplicate at the session change point (reload_drawings and the drawing-commit paths emitting drawings_changed) to exactly one all-view sync per change, reducing each pop-out _on_drawings_changed to a single-view refresh of its receiving view. Signal and per-pop-out wiring kept (A125); update semantics unchanged. Covers S-P13-4, AC-D49.4.
acceptance_criteria: Given the current tree before the dedupe change, when the pinning tests run, then they record the per-change all-view sync count and the end-state view contents as the baseline.

Given N open pop-outs on one symbol, when drawings change or reload offscreen, then sync_drawings_to_views executes exactly once per change with end state identical to the pinned baseline, while the drawings_changed signal and per-pop-out wiring remain connected.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given the current tree before the dedupe change, when the pinning tests run, then they record the per-change all-view sync count and the end-state view contents as the baseline.
tests.description: Spy on sync_drawings_to_views, open N pop-outs on one symbol, emit a drawing change, record call count and per-view end state into the pinned baseline assertions. Lands FIRST on the current tree (green-first, not red-first).
tests.expected_result: Green on the current tree; the recorded count/state become the baseline T42 asserts against.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given N open pop-outs on one symbol, when drawings change or reload offscreen, then sync_drawings_to_views executes exactly once per change with end state identical to the pinned baseline, while the drawings_changed signal and per-pop-out wiring remain connected.
tests.description: Same N-pop-out scenario post-dedupe: assert sync count is exactly 1 per change, per-view end state equals the T41 baseline, and the signal/slots remain connected (handler reduced to single-view refresh). Red without the dedupe (count N).
tests.expected_result: Fails without the dedupe (count N, not 1); passes post-fix with baseline-equal end state.

tasks.title: Shared-hold lifecycle probe with committed verification record, no prod change (D49.5 probe)
tasks.description: Write and run the offscreen hold-count verification probe across the shared-hold lifecycle (main-chart same-symbol reload, pop-out attach/close, zero-owner case asserting zero) and commit the verdict to docs/p13_hold_probe_record.md: whether the hold count exceeds active owners with a lasting effect (a duplicate live subscription surviving session use) or not. No production-code change in this task. Covers the W5 half of S-P13-5, AC-D49.5.
acceptance_criteria: Given the shared-hold lifecycle (main-chart same-symbol reload plus pop-out attach/close, plus a zero-owner case), when the probe runs offscreen, then it records the hold count against active owners at each step and states whether a lasting over-count effect exists.
Given the completed probe, when the tree is inspected, then docs/p13_hold_probe_record.md exists with the verdict and counts, and no production file outside tests and the record is modified.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given the shared-hold lifecycle (main-chart same-symbol reload plus pop-out attach/close, plus a zero-owner case), when the probe runs offscreen, then it records the hold count against active owners at each step and states whether a lasting over-count effect exists.
tests.description: Lifecycle probe: main-chart same-symbol reload, pop-out attach/close, and a zero-owner case asserting hold zero; assert hold count versus active owners at each step and write the lasting-effect-or-clean verdict. Always lands (the probe is the deliverable).
tests.expected_result: Green with a committed verdict either way; a missing verdict or unasserted zero-owner case fails.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given the completed probe, when the tree is inspected, then docs/p13_hold_probe_record.md exists with the verdict and counts, and no production file outside tests and the record is modified.
tests.description: Assert the record file exists naming per-step hold/owner counts and the explicit verdict line (lasting effect confirmed vs no lasting effect), and that the verdict vocabulary matches exactly one of the two specified outcomes.
tests.expected_result: Green once the record is committed; missing file, missing counts, or an ambiguous verdict fails.

tasks.title: Conditional per-owner hold fix, else verified-close on the probe record (D49.5 fix)
tasks.description: Read docs/p13_hold_probe_record.md (P13-T5) and act exactly on its verdict: if it confirms a lasting over-count effect, implement idempotent per-owner acquire/release (owners: main chart, each pop-out, alarm monitor) so the hold count equals active owners across the probe lifecycle; if it records no lasting effect, make NO production change and close D49.5 as verified (A126) citing the record. A diff here with no probe record fails review (R98). Covers the W6 half of S-P13-5, AC-D49.5.
acceptance_criteria: Given the P13-T5 probe record verdict, when the tree is inspected, then the tree state matches the verdict: a confirmed lasting effect yields idempotent per-owner acquire/release with the hold count equal to active owners across the probe lifecycle, while a clean verdict yields no production-code change to the hold accounting.
Given the final tree, when the hold lifecycle suites re-run, then they are green with no skips or xfails in any P13 hold test.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given the P13-T5 probe record verdict, when the tree is inspected, then the tree state matches the verdict: a confirmed lasting effect yields idempotent per-owner acquire/release with the hold count equal to active owners across the probe lifecycle, while a clean verdict yields no production-code change to the hold accounting.
tests.description: Read the record verdict inside the test: on confirmed, re-run the probe lifecycle and assert hold equals active owners with idempotent double-acquire/release safety; on clean, assert the hold-accounting code paths are unchanged from the probed baseline. No skip in either branch.
tests.expected_result: Fails if the tree contradicts the record verdict in either direction; green when tree and verdict agree.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given the final tree, when the hold lifecycle suites re-run, then they are green with no skips or xfails in any P13 hold test.
tests.description: Re-run the P13-T5 probe suites plus this task's fix suites against the final tree and scan the P13 hold test files for skip/xfail markers.
tests.expected_result: Green re-run with zero markers; any red suite or marker fails.

tasks.title: Thread the main-chart timezone offset into pop-out creation (D49.6 create)
tasks.description: Change ui/main_window.py _open_popout to pass the main chart's current self._tz_offset into the new PopoutChartWindow (removing the hardcoded tz_offset=0.0 at the creation call site in ui/popout_window.py), so the new view is constructed with the main chart's offset through the unchanged create_chart_view seam. Covers the create half of S-P13-6, AC-D49.6.
acceptance_criteria: Given a main chart with a non-zero timezone offset, when a pop-out is created offscreen, then the new view is constructed with the main chart's current offset and never the hardcoded 0.0.

Given the chart-view seam and the main-chart offset source, when inspected, then the create_chart_view signature is unchanged and self._tz_offset remains the single offset source (no new timezone source introduced).

tasks.title: Persist the offset with the pop-out set and restore it with fallback (D49.6 persist/restore)
tasks.description: Persist tz_offset in data/popout_store.py PopoutStore via an additive nullable column (pre-change rows read back without the field), thread it through save/load_all, and apply the stored offset at restore in _restore_popouts with the A134 fallback: a pre-change save without the field restores with the main chart's current offset, never silent UTC. Restored views render identical time labels for the same seeded bars. Covers the persist/restore half of S-P13-6, AC-D49.6.
acceptance_criteria: Given a saved pop-out set carrying a persisted offset, when it is restored offscreen, then the restored view carries the stored offset and renders identical time labels for the same seeded bars as the main chart.
Given a pre-change saved pop-out set without the offset field, when it is restored offscreen, then the restored view carries the main chart's current offset and never a silent UTC default.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given a saved pop-out set carrying a persisted offset, when it is restored offscreen, then the restored view carries the stored offset and renders identical time labels for the same seeded bars as the main chart.
tests.description: Save a pop-out set with a non-zero offset, restore offscreen, assert the restored view offset equals the stored value and its formatted time labels for seeded bars equal the main chart labels. Red pre-fix (no persisted field).
tests.expected_result: Fails pre-fix; passes post-fix with label equality.

tests.linked_acceptance_criterion: Given a pre-change saved pop-out set without the offset field, when it is restored offscreen, then the restored view carries the main chart's current offset and never a silent UTC default.
tests.description: Restore a legacy record lacking the field (migration read-back), assert the restored offset equals the main chart current offset and is not 0.0-under-a-nonzero-main.
tests.expected_result: Green post-fix; silent-UTC fallback fails it.
